summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with fever and hematuria. He had recently presented to the ED for hematuria, completed a dialysis session, and returned with fever and chills. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection caused by Escherichia coli, confirmed by urine culture. He was initially treated with IV levofloxacin and meropenem, then transitioned to ceftriaxone after developing itchy eyes on ciprofloxacin. He remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with negative blood cultures. A renal ultrasound showed no abscesses. He received scheduled dialysis during admission and was discharged home on oral cefpodoxime with follow-up planned in urology and orthopedics for persistent hematuria and chronic hip pain.
